title: Abstaining for a Brother, and One Body
english: For it is lawful to eat meat and to drink wine, but freedom in these things is not altogether without harm (Romans 14:21). Abstaining is also useful, so that we do not fatten the flesh with soft living and make the passions within it rage wild against ourselves. If, then, we abstain from these things for our own sake, much more for our brother’s, so that he may not stumble, because of the saying, “You shall love your neighbour as yourself” (Leviticus 19:18).

“Therefore receive one another, as Christ also received you, for the glory of God” (Romans 15:7). We who are many are one body, and members of one another, as it is written (Romans 12:5), since Christ binds us together into unity with the bonds of love: “For He Himself is the one who made both one and broke down the dividing wall of partition, abolishing the law of commandments in ordinances” (Ephesians 2:14–15). So we must be of the same mind toward one another (Romans 12:16); and if one member suffers, all the members must suffer with it, and if one member is honoured, all the members must rejoice (1 Corinthians 12:26). That is why he says, “Receive one another, as Christ also received you, for the glory of God.” And we shall receive one another if we choose to be of the same mind, bear one another’s burdens (Galatians 6:2), and keep “the unity of the…”

ἀζήμιον: 'without harm'.
δι' ἑαυτούς: 'for our own sake'.

title: Christ the Servant of the Promise
english: …“of the Spirit in the bond of peace” (Ephesians 4:3). So too God has received us in Christ (Romans 15:7). For he spoke the truth who said that the world was so loved by God the Father that the Son Himself was given for us (John 3:16). For He was given as the price exchanged for the life of us all, and by death we have obtained reconciliation, and we have been redeemed from death and sin.

And Paul makes clear the aim of the economy when he says that Christ became a servant of the circumcision for the sake of the truth, and the rest (Romans 15:8). For since God had promised beforehand to the fathers of the Jews that He would bless the offspring that was to come from them, and that it would be “like the stars of heaven in number” (Genesis 22:17), for this reason the Word, being God, appeared in the flesh and became man. He is the very one who holds all creation together in being and, as God, grants well-being to all that exists. He came into this world with flesh, yet, as He Himself says, not to be served, “but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many” (Matthew 20:28).
Yet He plainly confessed that He had come to fulfil the promise to Israel, for He said, “I was sent only to the lost…” (Matthew 15:24)

Ends mid-quotation at ἀπολωλότα; u11-rem-close begins πρόβατα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ. The closing ellipsis marks the break; the citation is placed at the break.
PG column number 248 is dropped from the reading text.
ἀληθὴς ... εἰπών: 'he who said is truthful'; the speaker of John 3:16 is not named by Cyril and is left as 'he'.
ἀντάλλαγμα: 'what is given in exchange'; rendered 'the price exchanged'.

καὶ θανάτου τὴν καταλλαγὴν ἐσχήκαμεν: the genitive is taken as means, 'by death we have obtained reconciliation'; compare Romans 5:10–11 (κατηλλάγημεν ... διὰ τοῦ θανάτου; τὴν καταλλαγὴν ἐλάβομεν), a possible echo noted only.
τὸν ... τῆς οἰκονομίας σκοπόν: οἰκονομία is the saving plan of the Incarnation; kept as 'economy'. The subject of διαλευκαίνει is Paul, named in English.
ὁ πᾶσαν τὴν κτίσιν καὶ εἰς τὸ εἶναι συνέχων: possible echo of Colossians 1:17 (τὰ πάντα ἐν αὐτῷ συνέστηκεν); noted only.
ψυχή in the Matthew quotation is rendered 'life', as the verse requires.

title: Mercy Widened to the Nations
english: …sheep of the house of Israel” (Matthew 15:24). So Paul does not speak falsely when he says that Christ became a servant from the circumcision to confirm the promises made to the fathers (Romans 15:8), and that besides this He was appointed by God the Father for mercy also to those from the nations, so that they too might glorify the Saviour and Redeemer as the Maker and Craftsman of all things (Romans 15:9).

For it was needful, truly needful, since the circumcision in its great disobedience insulted Him wickedly and would not accept the redemption He gave, that the unspeakable grace of God should not seem to have achieved nothing, when those from Israel who had believed and been saved were few, a bare handful. For this reason, as the calm that comes from above was spread wide, as it were, over all, the nations were received. And the mystery of the wisdom that is in Christ is seen not to have missed its aim, an aim set on kindness. For in place of those who had slipped, the whole world under heaven has been saved, because God had compassion.
And that the mystery had been proclaimed beforehand by the voice of holy men who foreknew in the Spirit what was to come, he establishes by setting out the prophecies most plainly (Romans 15:9–12).
translator_notes: Opens mid-quotation: εἰ μὴ εἰς τὰ ἀπολωλότα ends u11-rem-mid; this section supplies πρόβατα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ. The leading ellipsis marks the join.
Page numbers 31 and 32 in the copy-text are dropped from the reading text.
εἰς ἔλαιον: the copy-text reads ἔλαιον ('oil'); taken as ἔλεον ('mercy'), the sense of Romans 15:9 (ὑπὲρ ἐλέους) which Cyril is paraphrasing. Rendered 'for mercy'.
διάκονον αὐτὸν γεγενῆσθαι: the subject αὐτόν is Christ, named in English.
γενεσιουργὸν καὶ τεχνίτην: 'author of coming-to-be and craftsman'; rendered 'Maker and Craftsman of all things' (τῶν ὅλων).
ἔδει γὰρ ἔδει: the doubled verb is Cyril's emphasis, kept as 'it was needful, truly needful'.
ἡ ὑπ' οὐρανόν: the feminine article implies γῆ or οἰκουμένη ('the land/world under heaven'); rendered 'the whole world under heaven'.
κατοικτείροντος Θεοῦ: genitive absolute, rendered 'because God had compassion'.
ἁγίων ... ἐν πνεύματι: the holy prophets foreknew by the Holy Spirit; 'Spirit' is capitalized.
The fragment ends with Cyril's reference to the prophecies of Romans 15:9–12; they are not quoted here.
